questions.q: _______ insert new variables between existing variables.
questions.explanation: The number 2 points to the 'Insert Variable' toolbar icon, which allows you to add a new column (variable) between existing ones.

questions.q: This command allows reverse coding, and it makes data entry much more efficient (_______).
questions.explanation: The number 1 points to the 'Value Labels' button, which toggles between showing the underlying numeric values and their assigned string labels, making data entry verification efficient.

questions.q: _______ insert new cases between existing cases.
questions.explanation: The number 3 points to the 'Insert Cases' toolbar icon, which allows you to insert a new row (case) between existing data entries.

questions.q: _______ allows you to select which toolbars you want to show, select font size, add or remove the gridlines that separate each piece of data, and to select whether or not to display your raw data or the data labels.
questions.explanation: The number 5 points to the 'View' menu, which contains layout settings including toolbars, fonts, gridlines, and data label display toggles.

questions.q: _______ includes all of the commands to carry out statistical analyses and to calculate descriptive statistics. Much of this book will focus on using commands located in this menu.
questions.explanation: The number 4 points to the 'Analyze' menu, which is the primary location for running statistical tests, models, and descriptive statistics in SPSS.

questions.q: _______ includes the typical cut, copy, and paste commands, and allows you to specify various options for displaying data and output.
questions.explanation: The number 6 points to the 'Edit' menu, which provides standard clipboard utilities (cut, copy, paste) along with global options settings.

questions.q: _______ includes all of the options you typically use in other programs, such as open, save, exit. Notice, that you can open or create new files of multiple types as illustrated to the right.
questions.explanation: The number 7 points to the 'File' menu, which handles file creation, open, save, import, and exit operations.
